summary: Phase 4 of the myidsan productization plan ("Operability"): age-based retention for the append-only security audit log, plus a fix -- found by a live bench against a real Keycloak 26 realm -- that closes an auditing gap in federated (OIDC/social) login. A new audit config block (off by default) adds the one sanctioned exception to the trail's otherwise total lack of a delete path: maxRetentionDays (default 365, hard 30-day floor -- a lower configured value is raised and a startup warning logged), frequencyHours (default 24), and archiveDir (default audit-archive). A new IAuditService.PurgeOlderThan archives every row past the cutoff to a JSON-lines file, fsyncs and renames it into place, and only then deletes those rows from the table -- a run that cannot finish its archive deletes nothing -- then records the purge back into the trail it just trimmed (action audit.retention_purge, naming the cutoff, row count, and archive file) so a reader who finds history starting abruptly can tell a deliberate trim from an empty past. Wired as a new periodic scheduler task (myidsan-audit-retention), a no-op unless enabled. Separately, the bench found that providerCallback (the OIDC/Google/GitHub callback handler) audited only successful federated sign-ins: every refused SSO attempt -- a tampered state, a callback missing its flow cookies, an IdP-reported unverified email, a session-issue failure -- was invisible on the Audit log page while a refused password login was recorded. All four rejection paths now record a login.failure entry naming the provider and, where known, the account; the identity-provider unverified-email error also now names the address so the audit record identifies which account was refused. Federated failures deliberately do not advance the per-IP/per-account failed-login lockout, since the credential was checked at the IdP, not guessed against myidsan -- a misconfigured provider (clock skew, rotated secret) must not be able to lock real users out. A live bench against a real Samba AD DC found the same auditing gap in the Kerberos handler: a REJECTED SPNEGO ticket only incremented a Prometheus counter and left no audit record, while a rejected LDAP password login was recorded, so a forged or replayed ticket was invisible on the Audit log page. Refused tickets and unadmitted principals now write a login.failure entry carrying the reason and, where the ticket verified, the principal; a request carrying NO token still does not, because that is the first half of every SPNEGO handshake and auditing it would add one entry per browser request and bury the real rejections. Kerberos failures likewise do not advance the failed-login lockout: a ticket is verified against the keytab rather than guessed, and a keytab gone stale after a machine-account password rotation would otherwise lock out every domain user at once.
compatibility: audit.retention.enabled defaults false, so no existing install starts trimming its audit trail without an explicit config change; an install that never adds the block keeps every row forever, exactly as before. archiveDir resolves relative to the data directory and its files are written plaintext (0600, not at-rest sealed) -- back that directory up with the same care as the database once retention is turned on. The audit-log auditing fix is a pure bug fix with no configuration surface: existing federated logins are unaffected, refused ones simply now leave a record where none existed before, and no lockout behavior changes for any existing account. No schema changes; the purge writes to the same audit_log table via the existing repo, and archived rows are fully reconstructable from the JSON-lines archive file if ever needed. The Kerberos auditing fix is likewise a pure bug fix with no configuration surface: successful SPNEGO logins are unchanged, refused ones now leave a record, the SPNEGO challenge handshake is unaffected, and no lockout behaviour changes.
